issue_context.title: AEMET OpenData weather entity does not show units correctly. They are correct in sensor values
issue_context.body:
### The problem

The units shown in the weather entity (aemet daily) are not correct in the "Presión del aire" and "Velocidad del viento" values.

In this entity, the units are Pa for "Presión del aire" and m/s for "Velocidad del viento", that are not correct.

The correct ones are the units given by the two following entities:

sensor.aemet_pressure: The units are "hPa".
sensor.aemet_wind_speed: The units are "km/h".


Some images attached:

weather.aemet_daily:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/9607218/159921285-2aea9f16-b798-4724-88ff-a7429e4f56c5.png)

sensor.aemet_pressure:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/9607218/159921384-87fa6843-84e9-468d-ae34-c0c855abe392.png)

sensor.aemet_wind_speed:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/9607218/159921446-392ca866-0871-4ee4-8eeb-6fe1ca788261.png)



As the previous issue with the same title was closed without a solution, I create a new one (I cannot force re-open it)

review_comments:
Changing these keys, will change the unique_id of the `sensors` provided by this integration (and thus a breaking change).

The breaking change should be avoided. Either by not renaming the keys, or by providing a migration for existing entity entries in the registry.
Thanks a lot @frenck , fixed now to avoid breaking.

We shouldn't change keys or entity unique_id. These keys should be independent of the weather entity api. The keys should be integration specific, connected to the 3rd party api the integration is using.
You're right, the change of the unique_id is not motivated.
